item.title: Fatal parking lot crash in Nanaimo lands driver $1,000 in fines
item.description: A driver in a fatal crash in Nanaimo where an 85-year-old woman was killed while walking in a parking lot has been fined $1,000.

item.title: 'Targeting the most vulnerable': GVTA calls on board to cut administrative costs instead
item.description: The association says the province should shift the hundreds of millions it's positioned to give to private schools to the public system.

item.title: 'Forgotten population': People with special needs lose housing in Cowichan
item.description: A "shocking" funding cut has crushed plans to build affordable housing for people with special needs in the Cowichan Valley.

item.title: Future Luxton Fairgrounds revitalization dependent on more volunteers
item.description: The Metchosin Farmers' Institute is looking to give the historic Luxton Fairgrounds a facelift, however revitalization efforts are dependent on more volunteers.

item.title: 'We still don't know': Questions remain 20 years after Queen of the North sinking, says TSB head investigator
item.description: Reflecting on the fatal sinking of the MV Queen of the North, the former head of major investigations for the Transportation Safety Board says many lessons were learned.

item.title: Union president asks Canada Post workers to reject tentative agreement
item.description: The head of the union representing 55,000 Canada Post workers is calling for the employees to reject a tentative contract agreement in a vote this spring, even though a majority of the national executive board recommend that the deal be accepted.

item.title: U.K. midwife faces deportation after visa denied over English test
item.description: A Victoria midwife from the United Kingdom is facing deportation after her visa was refused because of a problem with her paperwork.

item.title: Family remembers Victoria man, Chuck Spence, killed in workplace incident
item.description: The family of a Victoria man, 50-year-old Chuck Spence, remember the husband and father who was killed in a workplace incident Monday.

item.title: Hollywood actor takes humorous look at Comox Valley gardening in new Netflix series
item.description: Zach Galifianakis of The Hangover fame lives in the Comox Valley and spoke with children and farmers for a new Netflix series premiering next month.

item.title: Vancouver Island’s Long Beach named one of the world’s top long beaches
item.description: Vancouver Island’s Long Beach has earned international recognition, landing on NDTV Travel’s list of the world’s most remarkable long beaches.

item.title: Carney says Air Canada CEO's English-only condolences lacked compassion
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney says the Air Canada CEO's English-only message of condolence after Sunday's deadly crash in New York lacked compassion.

item.title: Tofino shutting down section of road near elementary school due to ‘safety concerns’
item.description: The District of Tofino is closing down a section of Gibson Street to traffic following “ongoing safety concerns” in the area.

item.title: ‘Destroyed our patio’: Wind knocks trees onto cars, houses in Nanaimo
item.description: Strong winds wreaked havoc in Nanaimo on Tuesday, toppling trees onto cars, homes and across electric wires.

item.title: Canada is losing more air traffic controllers than it's hiring: aviation expert
item.description: An aviation expert says Canada is losing more air traffic controllers to retirement than it is hiring, despite efforts to ramp up recruitment.

item.title: CRD temporarily closes Thetis Lake main beach washrooms
item.description: Thetis Lake Regional Park trail users won't be able to access the main beach washroom facilities starting March 30 when they'll temporarily close for repairs.
